newsitem.title: USA: U.S. refiners pay highly for light, sweet crude.
newsitem.headline: U.S. refiners pay highly for light, sweet crude.

text.p: U.S. refiners facing limited availability of Brent-related crude due to a closed arbitrage are paying high premiums for imported light, sweet grades.
"Refiners in Corpus Christi (Texas) who have to import are paying up," a Midwest refiner said, noting some refiners with limited upgrading were subject to rising European prices.
A Gulf Coast refiner was believed to have paid on Monday Dec West Texas Intermediate plus 50-55 cents cif for Brent, to arrive in the U.S. November 24-28.
Another refiner also took a Nov 24-28 Cusiana at Jan WTI plus 35 cents fob, confirming the bullish trend for sweets.
In contrast, sours were weaker in a more ample environment with nearby Latin American suppliers sourcing for outlets.
Traders said Venezuela and Mexico both had incremental spot barrels for sale, with some refiners already involved in term discussions for possibly higher volumes next year.
But heavy sweets were steady, with YPF selling a second cargo of Escalante for Nov 22-24 at a higher price than the previous sale to Petrobas, at WTI minus $3.12 a barrel fob.
Canadon Seco, another heavy sweet grade, was up for sale around WTI minus $1.95 fob, inclusive of lightering.
But Oriente was seen under pressure due to deteriorating quality, with prices for mid-Nov pegged at WTI minus $2.30.
In the U.S. after market, three full cargoes of Nov Brent traded at $24.80 a barrel, some 10 cents higher than London's IPE close. Partials for Dec Brent moved at $24.25/30 a barrel.
A Dec/Jan Brent intermonth spread traded at 70 cents.
